question: to the Commission Anja Arndt (ESN) Subject:
Application of the EU Methane Regulation to imports from non-EU countries during a possible suspension of sanctions from 1 January 2027

According to an article published in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) on 21 July 2026, while the Commission does not intend to postpone the EU Methane Regulation’s entry into force on 1 January 2027, it does intend to suspend the imposition of sanctions for a period of three years. What would be the legal and practical consequences of a suspension of sanctions on imports of oil, natural gas and coal from non-EU countries with effect from 1 January 2027, and can imports that do not meet the requirements of the Methane Regulation be rejected at the EU’s external borders as part of customs clearance or be prevented from being placed on the market after 1 January 2027, or will the continuation of such imports into the European Union be permitted, despite a possible breach of the Methane Regulation, for as long as the envisaged sanctions are suspended?
